newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Uralmash registers new share issue.
newsitem.headline: Russia Uralmash registers new share issue.

text.p: Russian Uralmash Industries, the holding company for one of Russia's biggest heavy equipment makers Uralmash, has placed a 450 million rouble share issue, Uralmash Industries spokesman Boris Khimich said on Thursday.
Khimich said a placement of 4.5 million shares, each with a face value of 100 roubles, began on Tuesday. He said the placement would end no later than June 5, 1998.
"The underwriters of this share issue are Flemings and CentreInvest. They will make the private placement of the issue on the international financial market," Khimich said.
The placement is expected to bring the company $40-50 million, which will be spent on reconstructing the plant's steel-smelting production.
AO Uralskiye Mashinostroitelnye Zavody was registered as the holding company for Uralmash in December 1996 and share consolidation was completed earlier this year.

Charter capital as of May 1997 was 1.5 billion roubles, divided between 12.25 million ordinary and 2.75 million preferred shares. Charter capital will increase to 1.95 billion roubles after the issue.
The company said early this month that it would list its shares on a foreign stock exchange in July, preparatory to launching a global depositary receipt programme.
Shares on the RTS-2 system of less liquid shares, where Uralmash was recently listed, were $7.50/$10.00 bid/ask at the close on Wednesday.

The company's major shareholders include AO Industrial Group Bioprocess-NIPEK (40 percent), Regent Pacific (14 percent), Brunswick (seven percent), Citibank, New Century Holdings, Troika-Dialog and Chase Manhattan Bank, each of which owns between one and three percent of shares.
Company management and employees each own three percent of shares.
